units.name: Past time
rules: Past simple: finished actions, habits, states and main events in a story. Emphatic: "I did enjoy it."
Past simple = finished time / specific moment ("sent six months ago"). Present perfect = time up to now or present result.
Past continuous: background actions, actions in progress at a moment, annoying habits with always. Past perfect: before another past moment.
Past perfect continuous: duration up to a past moment ("had been writing for ten years").
would = repeated past actions (not states); used to = past habits AND states. be/get used to + -ing = be familiar with.

units.name: Future time
rules: will = predictions, spontaneous decisions, offers, promises. be going to = intentions and predictions from present evidence.
Present continuous = arrangements. Present simple = timetables and fixed events.
Future continuous: in progress at a future time. Future perfect: completed before a future time. Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future time.
After when, while, once, as soon as, until, before: present tenses, NOT will.
be about to / on the point of / due to / is to: near or formal future. Future in the past: would, was going to, was due to.

units.name: Passives & causatives
rules: Use the passive when the agent is unknown, obvious, unimportant, or to put new information at the end, or for a formal style.
Impersonal passive: It is said that... / He is said to be... / There are reported to have been...
Two objects: Jill was given the tickets / The tickets were given to Jill. With explain & suggest: only 'to' version.
Avoid passive in perfect continuous / future continuous: use in progress, in training, on display, under construction...
Causative: have/get sth done (arranged or unfortunate experience). get sb to do, have sb do, have sb doing.

units.name: Modals & semi-modals
rules: Ability: can/could; managed to / was able to for one past occasion; couldn't have for past impossibility.
Obligation: must (personal), have to (external); mustn't = prohibition; don't have to / needn't = no obligation; needn't have done = did it but wasn't necessary.
Certainty: must/can't (strong); will/won't have; probability: should, ought to, may well; possibility: may, might, could.
Past: must have, can't have, might have, should have, could have + past participle.
Criticism: should have / ought to have; could/might have; will/would for annoying habits.

units.name: Conditionals
rules: Zero: if + present, present. First: if + present, will/imperative. Second: if + past, would. Third: if + past perfect, would have + pp.
Mixed: if + past perfect, would + base (past → present); if + past, would have + pp (present → past).
Inverted: Should + subject... / Were + subject to... / Had + subject + pp... (more formal).
as/so long as, provided/providing (that), on condition (that), supposing, unless, otherwise, in case.
But for / if it hadn't been for / Had it not been for + noun = without.

units.name: Unreal time
rules: Past tenses can refer to the present/future when unreal: wish, if only, as if/as though, would rather, it's (high/about) time, suppose/supposing/imagine.
wish + past simple (now) / past perfect (past regret) / would (annoyance or change) / could (ability).
It's (high) time + past simple: It's time we left. would rather + subject + past: I'd rather you didn't smoke. (same subject: would rather + base).
as if/as though + past = untrue now; present = possible. After was/were: 'were' is more formal; 'If I were you'.
We don't use would after wish when the subject of wish and would is the same person.

units.name: Adjectives & adverbs
rules: Order of adjectives: opinion, size, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose. "a lovely little wooden cabin".
Some adjectives only after the verb: afraid, alike, alive, alone, asleep, awake. After as/so/too/how: as crowded a city as...
Gradable (very, quite, fairly) vs ungradable (absolutely, completely, utterly): exhausted, perfect, impossible.
Comparatives: much/far/slightly + comparative; by far/easily + superlative; not nearly as... as; the + comparative, the + comparative.
Confusing forms: hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly, short/shortly, right/rightly.

units.name: Clauses
rules: Defining relative clauses: no commas; 'that' possible; pronoun can be omitted if it is the object. Non-defining: commas; no 'that'; pronoun cannot be omitted.
whom (formal object), whose (possessive), which can refer to the whole clause. Preposition + whom/which = formal.
Participle clauses: reduce relative clauses, give reasons, actions in sequence (Having finished..., Walking down the street...). Same subject in both parts.
Concession: although, though, even though, in spite of / despite + noun/-ing, whereas, while, however, much as, try as he might.
Even if = it doesn't matter whether; even though = despite the fact that.

units.name: Complex sentences
rules: Negative adverbials at the start → inversion: Never have I..., Hardly had... when..., No sooner had... than..., Not only did..., Rarely/Seldom do..., Little did he know...
Only after/only when/not until + inversion in the main clause: Only when he left did I realise...
On no account / under no circumstances / at no time / in no way + auxiliary + subject.
Cleft sentences: It was Carol who called. What annoys me is... The reason why... was... The place where...
so/such/too/enough: so + adj/adv + that; such + (a) noun + that; too + adj + to; adj + enough + to.

units.name: Noun phrases
rules: Countable / singular uncountable (advice, information, furniture, news) / plural uncountable (clothes, scissors, goods, savings).
Quantifiers: many/few/several/a number of + countable; much/little/an amount of + uncountable; a lot of/plenty of/some with both.
a few = some; few = hardly any; a little = some; little = hardly any.
a/an: first mention, classify. the: specific, unique, superlatives. Zero article: general plural/uncountable, institutions (go to school), meals, most countries.
the + adjective = group (the rich, the French). Group nouns can take singular or plural verbs.

units.name: Verbal complements
rules: + -ing: enjoy, avoid, admit, deny, consider, suggest, risk, resent, can't help, mind, practise, finish, feel like, look forward to.
+ to-infinitive: afford, agree, arrange, decide, expect, hope, manage, offer, plan, promise, refuse, seem, tend, threaten, wish.
verb + object + to: advise, allow, ask, encourage, force, persuade, remind, tell, warn. + bare infinitive: let, make (active), see/hear/watch.
Change in meaning: remember/forget/regret/stop/try/go on/mean + -ing vs to-infinitive.
Subjunctive: It's essential that he be informed / that she (should) arrive on time. Preparatory it: I consider it odd that...

units.name: Reporting
rules: Backshift: present → past, past simple/present perfect → past perfect, will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to.
No change for past perfect, could/would/should/might/ought to/had better, or when the information is still true.
Time/place words: now → then, today → that day, yesterday → the day before, tomorrow → the next day, here → there, this → that, ago → before.
Reported questions: no inversion, no question mark: She asked if/whether... / what time it was. Commands: told/ordered/asked + object + to-infinitive.
Reporting verbs: accuse sb of -ing, admit/deny/suggest -ing, promise/refuse/offer to, advise sb to, warn sb (not) to, insist on -ing, apologise for -ing, agree to.
